summary.en: Somali militants attacked an Ethiopian base, killing 43 soldiers, while Ethiopian forces engaged Eritrean-backed fighters in Gemalo near Badme and shelled Alamata, killing 14 civilians, according to Amnesty. Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed warned Eritrea to cease support for Ethiopia's enemies or face destruction, and reiterated Ethiopia will not invade Eritrea, while also reaffirming a commitment to Horn of Africa peace. Kenyan trucks were escorted across the volatile Moyale border and Ethiopian troops resumed flights to Aksum, as MPs raised alarms over civilian killings and displacement across Amhara, Oromia, Tigray and other regions. The conflict produced 2,824 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Somali-militante angrep en etiopisk base og drepte 43 soldater, mens etiopiske styrker møtte eritreisk-støttede kampere i Gemalo nær Badme og skjøt mot Alamata, der 14 sivile ble drept, ifølge Amnesty. Etiopias statsminister Abiy Ahmed advarte Eritrea om å stoppe støtten til Etiopias fiender eller risikere ødeleggelse, og gjentok at Etiopia ikke vil invadere Eritrea, samtidig som han bekreftet en forpliktelse til fred i Afrikas horn. Kenianske lastebiler ble eskortert over den ustabile Moyale-grensen, og etiopiske tropper gjenopptok flyvninger til Aksum, mens parlamentarikere varslet om sivile drap og fordrivelse i Amhara, Oromia, Tigray og andre regioner. Konflikten førte til 2 824 dødsfall i kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Fano insurgency
background.extract: The Fano insurgency or Amhara war is an armed conflict and insurgency in the Amhara Region of Ethiopia that began in April 2023 between the Fano militia and the Ethiopian government. The conflict started after the government attempted to dissolve the Amhara Special Forces and other regional forces as part of a plan to reform and centralize the country's security apparatus, and integrate them into the federal armed forces. This move led to protests and armed resistance by local forces under Fano.
